S.G. Pandit J., Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
Though this appeal is listed for admission, it is taken up for final disposal, with the consent of learned counsel for both the parties.

2. The Owner of offending motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-26/S-4123 is before this Court calling in question the correctness of judgment and award dated 05.01.2019 passed in MVC No.1704/2017 on the file of the learned II Addl.
Senior
Civil Judge and Member, MACT, Belagavi (for short, 'Tribunal'), fastening 50% liability to pay compensation on the appellant/owner and exonerating the Insurer from liability to pay compensation.

3. The claimants, who are the wife and minor children of the deceased Veerendra Angadi, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the accidental death of deceased Veerendra Angadi that took place on 14.07.2015 involving Suzuki Access motorcycle bearing registration No.KA- 25/EN-4172 and Bajaj Discover motorcycle bearing registration No. KA-26/S-4123.
It is stated that the deceased was aged about 39 years as on the date of the accident and he was working as SDA in Forest Department and drawing a salary of Rs.25,000/- per month.
appeared through their learned counsel.
Respondent No.2- insurer filed statement of objections denying entire allegations made in the claim petition.
It was contended that as on the date of the accident, insurance policy was not in force, therefore, insurer is not liable to pay compensation.
Thus, prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
5. Before the Tribunal, father of 1st claimant examined himself as PW1 and got marked the documents as Exs.P1 to P12.
Respondents did not examine any witness nor marked any documents.

The Tribunal based on the material evidence on record awarded total compensation of Rs.37,95,820/- with interest at 8% per annum holding that respondent No.2/Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation and respondent No.1/owner of the offending motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-26/S-4123 is liable to pay 50% of the compensation amount.

6. While awarding the above compensation, the Tribunal determined income of the deceased at Rs.20,699/- per month after deducting professional tax of Rs.200/-, deducted 1/3rd towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and applied multiplier of 15 taking the age of the deceased as 39 years.
The owner of the offending motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-26/S- 4123 is before this Court challenging 50% of liability saddled on him.

7. Heard Sri.S.M. Kalwad, learned counsel for the appellant-Owner as well as Sri.M.Y.Katagi,
learned counsel for the respondent-Insurance Company and perused the appeal papers along with original records.
8.

Sri .S.M. Kalwad, learned counsel for the appellant-Owner of offending motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-26/S-4123 with vehemence would contend that the Tribunal committed an error in holding that the accident occurred due to negligence of both riders of motorcycles in question.

He would submit that rider of motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-25/EN-4172 was coming from Gadag to Hulakoti on the left side of the road and rider of motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-26/S- 4123 came from opposite side and dashed.
It is his submission that due to sole negligence of rider of motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-25/EN-4172 i.e. deceased, the accident took place.
Thus, he prays for allowing the appeal by exonerating the appellant from liability to pay compensation.

9. Per contra, Sri.M.Y. Katagi, learned counsel appearing for the respondent-Insurance Company supporting the impugned judgment and award would contend that as on the date of the accident the insurance was not in existence.

He further submits that the Tribunal on appreciation of oral and documentary evidence is justified in holding that the accident had taken place due to contributory negligence on the part of the deceased Veerendra and rider of motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-26/S-4123.
Therefore, he submits that the impugned judgment and award does not call for interference at the hands of this Court.
Thus, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.

10. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the appeal papers, the only point that would fall for consideration in this appeal is, whether the Tribunal is justified in holding that the accident occurred due to contributory negligence of both riders of motorcycle in question?
11. Our answer to the above point is in the affirmative for the following reasons.

12. There is no dispute with regard to the accident occurred on 14.07.2015 involving Suzuki Access motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-25/EN-4172 and Bajaj Discover motorcycle bearing registration No. KA- 26/S-4123 resultant death of deceased Veerendra Angadi in this appeal.
The owner of the offending motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-26/S-4123 is before this Court questioning 50% liability saddled on him.

3 13.
Ex.P4-Spot Mahazar which discloses that the spot of the accident is Gadag-Hulakote road near Binkadakatti oil mill.

Ex.P5-Sketch of the spot of the accident discloses that rider of motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-25/EN-4172 i.e. deceased was coming from Gadag to Hulakoti and rider of motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-26/S-4123 was coming from Hulakoti to Gadag in opposite direction and the accident had taken place in the middle of the road.
It further discloses that due to fault on the part of both riders of motorcycles in question, the accident took place.
Moreover, charge sheet was filed against both riders of motorcycles in question.
A careful perusal of Ex.P5-Sketch would go to show that the accident occurred in the middle of the road and there was sufficient space on either side of the road.

The Tribunal on examination of material on record has given a categorical finding that both riders of motorcycles in question have contributed to the accident in question, which needs no interference.
14. Admittedly, as on the date of the accident, the offending motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-26/S- 4123 was not covered with insurance policy.
It is seen that the validity of insurance was from 19.4.2013 to 1.4.2014.
The alleged accident took place on 14.07.2015.
The claimants failed to produce any document to prove that as on the date of the accident, the insurance policy was in force.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly observed that the claimants have not discharged the burden of proving the existence of insurance policy as on the date of the accident.

Thus, the Tribunal is justified in holding that the respondent No.2/Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation and respondent No.1/Owner of the offending motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-26/S- 4123 is liable to pay 50% of the compensation amount.
We find no error in the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
Hence, we find no merit in the appeal and same is liable to be dismissed.

15. Hence, we pass the following:
ORDER a) Appeal stands dismissed as devoid of merit.
b) The amount in deposit shall be transmitted to the concerned Tribunal.
c) Registry to transmit the records to the Tribunal forthwith.
d) No order as to costs.
